findings.title: `caught_up` can report "yes" when the wanted range is unknown
findings.description:
When a product has a tier but the dataset edge has never been observed and `entry.end` is `None`, `_wanted_end` returns `None`, so `wanted` is `None`. `caught_up` is still called with `wanted=wanted_start is not None`, which is `True`. Scope then falls back to only the sessions already held.

`caught_up` ends in `all(...)` over those verdicts. With nothing held, that is vacuously `True`, so the report says `caught up: yes`. Even with some sessions held, the answer covers only those sessions, not the range the product wants. This is the silent fallback the project rules forbid. It is latent today because `TICK_UNIVERSE` has `tier=None`, but it will surface when a tier is configured before the first `pass` has observed an edge.

Treat "wanted configured but end unknown" as its own state. Return `None` or "unknown", or raise.

findings.title: `raw_counts` is not scoped to the product's shape
findings.description:
`raw_counts` counts every `tick_trade` row in the session windows, grouped by instrument. The ledger side (`ledger_totals`) is filtered to the product's shape. `build_coverage` runs once per universe entry, so a second product would fail the check in the first product's windows:
- Its instruments have raw rows but no ledger rows.
- They show up as mismatches (ledger 0, raw n), which makes `coverage` exit 3 falsely.

It works today only because `TICK_UNIVERSE` has one entry (`ES`). Restrict the raw scan to the product's instruments, for example by joining on the shape's ledger or definition instrument IDs, or document that coverage supports one product.

findings.title: Calendar error mapping duplicated
findings.description: `calendar_sessions` repeats the open/try/except/close pattern and the same error mapping as `product_session_days` in `tick_calendar.py:67-81`. Both map `psycopg.OperationalError` and `CalendarNotFoundError` to "unavailable" and `OutOfPopulatedRangeError` to a calendar error. The diff did refactor shared helpers elsewhere (`utc_midnight`, `days_touched`). The same treatment fits here, for example a shared `sessions_between` wrapper in `tick_calendar.py` that `product_session_days` also uses. Otherwise the two mappings will drift.

findings.title: Redundant `shape_units` query per product
findings.description: `_scope` calls `shape_units`, and `session_verdicts` immediately calls it again for the same shape and connection. Fetch it once and pass it in. The cost is small today, but it is wasted work.

findings.title: Untyped connection in the read helpers
findings.description: `_read` and the inner `read` in `tick_coverage` type the connection as `Any`, although `manifest_reads.Conn` exists and the build functions use it. Using `Conn` would keep strict pyright meaningful at this boundary.

findings.title: Long functions and short names
findings.description: `_product_lines` (about 55 lines) and `_product_status` (about 50 lines) are at the project's ~50-line limit. They also use single-letter names (`p`, `c`, `s`, `v`, `e`, `m`) outside short comprehensions. The `lines[-1] += ...` patch to the last bucket row is fragile. Splitting out the header, edge, bucket and contract sections would help.

findings.title: Exception handling and process-boundary mapping
findings.description: `run_mapped` is a documented process boundary that re-raises unmapped exceptions. The new `storage` parameter is narrow and explicit. `TickDatabaseUnreachable` is a specific subclass, so writer behavior is unchanged. `connect_migrated` closes the connection on any failure, and `_read` closes it in `finally`.

findings.title: Test coverage
findings.description: Tests cover the read helpers (including midnight-crossing raw counts), the build functions after real ingests, a deliberately deleted row producing a mismatch and exit 3, preflight exit 1, and unreachable database exit 4. The tests that previously left logging bound to CliRunner's stream now patch `setup_logging`.
